desc:
Given an array nums of non-negative integers and a positive integer k, decide whether some contiguous subarray of length at least 2 has a sum that is a multiple of k. A sum of 0 counts as a multiple of every k.

nums = [23, 2, 4, 6, 7], k = 6  -> true   ([2, 4] sums to 6)
nums = [23, 2, 6, 4, 7], k = 13 -> false
hints: Trying all pairs of ends works in O(n2) with prefix sums. Look for a way to ask the question about prefix sums modulo k.
A block from prefix i to prefix j has a sum divisible by k exactly when the two prefix sums leave the same remainder when divided by k.

Store, for each remainder, the earliest prefix index where it appeared (remainder 0 at index 0 before any element). When a remainder repeats, check that the two prefixes are at least 2 apart. Do not overwrite the stored index.
editorial: Let r_i be the prefix sum of the first i elements taken modulo k, with r_0 = 0. The subarray covering elements i..j-1 has a sum divisible by k if and only if r_i = r_j. The extra requirement is that the subarray has at least two elements, i.e. j - i ≥ 2.

Keep a dictionary from remainder to the first prefix index that produced it. When the current remainder is already present, the farthest possible partner is the first occurrence, so compare against it: if the gap is at least 2 you are done. If the gap is only 1, keep the old index (do not overwrite it) because the earliest index gives the longest subarray for later matches. One pass, O(n) time, and O(min(n, k)) space.
